title: mto-extension-vault-enterprise values
description: Deliberately minimal. This chart is normally rendered by template-operator-v2 from the bootstrap chart's valuesTemplate, so any constraint here has to accept everything t-op-v2 can send -- including serviceAccounts/deployments arriving as JSON null when a tenant has no workloads yet. Constrained: the switches consumed as string comparisons, because a near-miss there (yes / on / True / 1) silently disables a feature, and the token durations, because VCO takes them as integer seconds and a duration string would fail the whole TemplateInstance at apply. The boolean forms mirror the bootstrap chart's _helpers.tpl: a boolean, or the quoted strings "true"/"false".

boolish.description: true or false, as a YAML boolean or as the quoted string "true"/"false". yes, on, off, 1, 0, True and TRUE are rejected, because they would be read as "not enabled" without warning.

seconds.description: Whole seconds. vault-config-operator's KubernetesAuthEngineRole types these fields as integers, so "1h" renders clean and is rejected at apply. 0 means Vault's default.

comment-on-component: `component` is deliberately NOT constrained here. templates/_helpers.tpl already fails on an unknown component with a message naming the valid set, and a schema enum would pre-empt it with a vaguer error while duplicating the valid list in a second place.

eso.description: A string, not a boolean: "enabled" or "disabled".

token.description: Workload token settings stamped onto every KubernetesAuthEngineRole. `type` is enumerated because Vault's default/default-service/default-batch resolve against the auth mount's tune, making token semantics depend on state this chart does not own. numUses is deliberately absent: Vault accepts it on a batch token and ignores it.

type.description: service persists the token (renewable, revocable, enumerable). batch is never stored (no renewal and no revocation). Pair batch with a short ttl.
